DECISION (Wilson, 2026-09-21, answered "2" to the 3 options presented after the qualification-probe finding): proceed with prompt-blind subagent arms, same posture as M007. Explicitly accepts:
(a) no hook enforcement for these arms (confirmed by the qualification probe, addendum #1);
(b) NO TRANSCRIPT AUDIT is available for this mechanism either. M007's transcript audits (fde/inspect_run.py --transcript) worked because those runs were separate `claude -p` subprocesses via run_blind.sh with an on-disk transcript file the orchestrator could scan. Subagents dispatched via this session's Agent tool produce a JSONL transcript the orchestrator is instructed not to read or grep, even after completion (a harness-level restriction, not a project one). So unlike M007, ES3 (isolation breach) cannot be checked by transcript audit for these arms; the only evidence of blindness is the subagent's own self-report and the Kernel's own access-scoped context construction (ctx_rN.json already excludes tier>=4/quarantined content and ground truth by construction, independent of blindness). This is a real reduction in rigor versus the design v3 was written for, and it is disclosed rather than worked around.
Mechanism going forward: driver_m008.py init <run> M008 <mode> --scored (v3 active, run_manifest.json records run_kind=scored + registration_hash + code_hashes), one subagent per run dispatched foreground, one run at a time (per Wilson's standing instruction), scored with driver_m008.py score after each, checked against ES1/ES2/ES4. K1/K2 findings from these runs must be reported with this disclosure attached, not as if hook-enforced or transcript-audited blindness stood behind them.
